articles.title: 'Agudo grave' de Zélia Duncan se abre na pulsação transformadora de show com direção musical de Maria Beraldo | G1
articles.body:
Zélia Duncan reconstrói hits como 'Catedral' e 'Nos lençóis desse reggae' com a renovadora textura sonora do show 'Agudo grave' — Foto: Rodrigo Goffredo

Data e local: 25 de setembro de 2026 na casa Vivo Rio (Rio de Janeiro, RJ)

♬ Zélia Duncan deu passo à frente no álbum “Agudo grave” , 15º disco de estúdio da cantora, compositora e instrumentista fluminense em 45 anos de carreira iniciada em Brasília (DF) em 1981. O movimento foi articulado em conexão com Maria Beraldo, produtora musical e arranjadora do álbum “Agudo grave” .

No show homônimo que estreou em 4 de setembro em São Paulo (SP) e que chegou ao Rio de Janeiro (RJ) na noite de sexta-feira, 25 de setembro, Zélia expande esse movimento sob direção musical da mesma Maria Beraldo. Em cena, o “Agudo grave” de Zélia Duncan se abre e se amplifica no sopro transformador de arranjos que renovam as músicas do repertório pregresso da cantora.

Terceira música na disposição de roteiro, “Me revelar” (Christiaan Oyens e Zélia Duncan, 2001), por exemplo, ganha outra pulsação. Até “Catedral” (“Cathedral song” – Tanita Tikaran, 1988, em versão em português de Christiaan Oyens, 1994), música que catapultou a cantora ao estrelato em 1994, é reconstruída na cena leve e inventiva do show “Agudo grave”, com direito ao sopro do clarone de Maria Beraldo na estreia carioca do show na casa Vivo Rio.

Zélia Duncan assina a direção do show 'Agudo grave' em parceria com a cenógrafa Simone Mina — Foto: Rodrigo Goffredo

Moldada pela banda formada por Aline Gonçalves (flautas e clarinete), Amanda Camargo (piano), Antonio Loureiro (bateria), Ciro Bellucci (violões) e Fabio Sá (baixo), todos músicos que são multi-instrumentistas, a textura sonora dos arranjos de Maria Beraldo se situa no território da experimentação, mas no limite da acessibilidade pelo público que segue Zélia desde 1994, ano da projeção nacional da cantora.

Maleável, essa textura sonora serve bem tanto à concretude urbana de “Olhos de cimento” (Pedro Luís e Zélia Duncan, 2026), número de pressão quase roqueira, quanto à delicadeza da paisagem solar em que se ambienta “Meu plano” (2026), parceria de Zélia com Ná Ozzetti.

Ficou evidente no álbum “Agudo grave” que nem todas as músicas do repertório autoral estavam à altura da sonoridade arrojada do disco. Essa sensação ainda permanece no show, em uma ou outra música, como “Importante” (Alberto Continentino e Zélia Duncan, 2026), mas em menor grau.

O repertório do álbum cresce no show dirigido pela própria Zélia Duncan em parceria com Simone Mina, criadora do cenário que traduz em imagens – móbiles que parecem cristais aos olhos do público – a fluidez e a leveza do show, ainda que haja certo peso na batida quase marcial da bateria de Antonio Loureiro em “Sentidos” (Christiaan Oyens e Zélia Duncan, 1994), uma das músicas antigas que dão a sensação de que tudo soa novo de novo na voz da cantora.

“Pontes no ar” (Zélia Duncan e Alberto Continentino, 2016), da safra nova, é música erguida no show com arranjo que parece fazer volitar a canção evocativa da atmosfera do Clube da Esquina, sobretudo do cancioneiro pop folk de Lô Borges (1952 – 2025).

Na cena, o gestual teatral da cantora – que já atuou como atriz, cabe lembrar – realça o sentido dos versos de músicas como “E aí, IA?” (2026), outra das três parcerias de Zélia Duncan com Alberto Continentino que fazem parte do repertório do álbum “Agudo grave”.

Zélia Duncan apresenta o show 'Agudo grave' ao público carioca na casa Vivo Rio, na noite de sábado, 25 de setembro — Foto: Rodrigo Goffredo

Outro parceiro de Zélia no álbum “Agudo grave” , Lenine injetou vitalidade no show ao entrar em cena para cantar com a anfitriã “Maravilha disforme” (2026) e uma canção de lavra solitária, “Meu xamego” (2025), antes de voltar para o bis para se juntar a Zélia e a Maria Beraldo na viagem refrescante pelo reggae “Nos lençóis desse reggae” (Christiaan Oyens e Zélia Duncan, 1994).

Novas ou antigas, como a sempre aliciante “Enquanto durmo” (Christiaan Oyens e Zélia Duncan, 1996), as músicas se harmonizam na cena do show “Agudo grave”, quebrando a barreira do tempo e sinalizando que o tempo de Zélia Duncan é hoje.

“Calmo” (2026), parceria da artista com Zeca Baleiro, é cantada em clima de intimidade, com Zélia sentada na beira do palco, próxima da plateia. “Capitu” (Luiz Tatit, 1999) – música que Ná Ozzetti lançou no álbum “Estopim” (1999) e que Zélia Duncan tomou para si em gravação feita para o álbum “Eu me transformo em outras” (2004) – navegou poderosa pela ressaca dos mares do novo arranjo.

“Matagal” (2024), canção em inglês composta por Maria Beraldo e lançada pela autora há dois anos em feat com Zélia, se afinou com o tom inusual dos arranjos e, nesse clima, é claro que caberia música de Itamar Assumpção (1949 – 2023), compositor de obra vanguardista abordada por Zélia Duncan com assiduidade e devoção há 30 anos. “Tua boca” (Itamar Assumpção, 1993) é sugada pela cantora no show “Agudo grave” de forma sedutora.

Zélia Duncan (à esquerda) canta com Maria Beraldo, diretora musical do show 'Agudo grave', na apresentação da casa Vivo Rio — Foto: Rodrigo Goffredo

A propósito, as incursões feitas por Zélia Duncan em território alheio são todas frutíferas. Pérola do aclamado álbum “Blue” (1971), obra-prima da discografia da cantora e compositora canadense Joni Mitchell, norte da estrada folk percorrida por Zélia, a canção “All I want” refaz o convite à dança, à liberdade e ao risco de amar.

“Pan y leche” (1995), canção em português (com um ou outro verso em espanhol) de Maurício Pereira, reforçou a busca da artista por felicidade e por seguir em frente em movimento progressista afinado com a estética do show, no qual a militante Zélia também marca posição política.

E, se a vida é sonho, a lembrança sagaz de “Sonho impossível” (“The impossible dream” – Joe Darion e Mitch Leigh, 1965, em versão em português de Chico Buarque e Ruy Guerra, 1972) – acoplada em medley com “Que tal o impossível?” (1988), música de Itamar Assumpção – arrebata no arremate do show.

E o fato é que, sim, sob a revigorante direção musical de Maria Beraldo, Zélia Duncan faz brotar uma flor do impossível chão do show “Agudo grave”.

articles.title: Conheça a banda mineira indicada ao Grammy Latino em 2026 | G1
articles.standfirst: Grupo concorre ao prêmio de Melhor Álbum de Música Cristã em Língua Portuguesa com o disco 'O Que Atravessa O Peito'. Cerimônia da 27ª edição do Latin Grammy será em 12 de novembro de 2026, nos EUA.
articles.summary: Grupo belo-horizontino Verboemcarne concorre ao prêmio de Melhor Álbum de Música Cristã em Língua Portuguesa com o disco "O Que Atravessa O Peito".
articles.body:
Uma banda de Belo Horizonte que mistura indie rock, música brasileira e reflexões sobre fé e vida contemporânea rompeu as divisas de Minas Gerais e está entre os indicados ao Grammy Latino 2026. Guilherme Januário, Michael Dias, Jordan Victor e Cris Duarte são só expectativa para viajar para os Estados Unidos e participar da cerimônia, em novembro.

A Verboemcarne (veja fotos ao fim da reportagem) concorre na categoria Melhor Álbum de Música Cristã em Língua Portuguesa com o disco "O Que Atravessa O Peito". Este é o segundo trabalho do grupo com gravação em estúdio.

O álbum indicado ao prêmio possui nove faixas . A banda aborda conflitos internos e a busca por espiritualidade em meio aos desafios da vida moderna. A sonoridade combina elementos do rock alternativo com influências da música brasileira.

"A gente lançou o trabalho, e a nossa produtora, a The Bow, nos inscreveu até sem a gente saber. Depois disso, a comissão do Grammy vê se o trabalho está apto. Se estiver tudo dentro dos critérios da academia, você é considerado. Nesse momento somos avisados e não podemos fazer campanha ou pedir votos, caso conheçamos algum membro. Após isso, eles passam por uma votação dos integrantes da academia, com mais de 7 mil pessoas, e aí saem os indicados", explicou o guitarrista Michael Dias.

Ainda segundo Michael, eles não estavam esperando a indicação. Também não acompanharam a divulgação que é feita pelas redes sociais do Grammy e por meio de uma nota.

"Outros amigos artistas que estavam esperando ligaram para o Guilherme, o vocalista. Estava cada um no seu trabalho. Guilherme ficou muito surpreso e emocionado e mandou no nosso grupo de WhatsApp a notícia. Ficamos felizes o dia inteiro, e à noite todo mundo foi lá para casa, pedimos uma pizza e comemoramos", contou.

O baixista Cris Duarte também afirmou que a indicação foi uma surpresa.

"Sabemos da qualidade desse trabalho e do quanto nos empenhamos para produzi-lo, mas realmente não esperávamos por isso", afirmou.

Banda de BH Verboemcarne é indicada ao Grammy Latino na categoria Melhor Álbum de Música Cristã em Língua Portuguesa com o disco "O Que Atravessa O Peito". — Foto: Divulgação

Três dos quatro integrantes se conheceram em 2018, numa fila pra um show de uma banda, com estilo parecido com a Verboemcarne. Guilherme Januário e Michael Dias se tornaram amigos e sempre tiveram a vontade de montar uma banda.

Naquela noite, os dois também conheceram o baterista Jordan Victor e começaram a acompanhar o trabalho dele nas redes sociais.

Em 2020, em plena pandemia, Guilherme e Michael decidem colocar o sonho em prática e montaram a Verboemcarne, com canções autorais. Em pouco tempo o projeto já dava sinais de que poderia crescer. Dois de quatro integrantes não quiseram continuar, e foi aí que a formação foi refeita e surgiu o convite para Jordan fazer parte.

Nascia, então, uma trajetória independente na cena musical de Belo Horizonte, sempre apostando em letras que carregam a fé como tema central. E, agora, os quatro integrantes fazem uma vaquinha para ir para a cerimônia do Grammy Latino, nos Estados Unidos.

A 27ª edição do Latin Grammy será realizada em 12 de novembro , em Las Vegas. A premiação reconhece gravações lançadas entre 1º de junho de 2025 e 31 de maio de 2026.

articles.title: Arlindo Cruz é celebrado por cantoras em EP que fica completo com a edição da gravação feita por Vanessa da Mata | G1
articles.body:
Arlindo Cruz (1958 – 2025), em foto de 2012, tem músicas regravadas pelas cantoras Agnes Nunes, Duda Beat, Luedji Luna, Ivete Sangalo e Vanessa da Mata — Foto: Zé Paulo Cardeal / Globo

♬ Com o lançamento da gravação em que Vanessa da Mata canta “O que é o amor” ( Arlindo Cruz , Maurição e Fred Camacho, 2007), quinta e última faixa do tributo fonográfico idealizado pelo produtor Liminha para celebrar Arlindo Cruz (14 de setembro de 1958 – 8 de agosto de 2025), o EP “Elas cantam Arlindo” ficou disponível na íntegra na sexta-feira, 25 de setembro.

Como o título “Elas cantam Arlindo” já explicita, o EP apresenta músicas do compositor carioca – bamba do samba da geração surgida com o grupo Fundo de Quintal entre o fim dos anos 1970 e o início da década de 1980 – nas vozes de cantoras. Além de Vanessa da Mata, o elenco feminino do EP é formado por Agnes Nunes, Duda Beat, Ivete Sangalo e Luedji Luna.

Agnes Nunes canta “Será que é amor?” (Arlindo Cruz, Babi e Junior Dom, 2003). Duda Beat dá voz ao samba “Agora viu que perdeu e chora” (Arlindo Cruz, Franco Lattari e Jorge David, 2012). Ivete Sangalo reaviva “Meu lugar” (Arlindo Cruz e Mauro Diniz, 2007). Já Luedji Luna interpreta “O bem” (Arlindo Cruz e Délcio Luiz, 2011).

A produção musical e a direção artística do EP “Elas cantam Arlindo” são assinadas por Liminha com Boris Farias.

articles.body: 'The Paradise' showed a slight improvement in its theatrical business on Saturday, September 26. The Nani and Kayadu Lohar-starrer registered a 2.3% rise in its India net collection compared with Day 2.According to Sacnilk, the action film earned Rs 15.25 cr nett on its third day. It had recorded Rs 14.90 cr nett on Friday. The latest collection takes its total India net earnings to Rs 76.40 cr. The movie also added Rs 4.00 cr from overseas markets on Saturday. Its cumulative overseas gross collection has reached Rs 29.00 cr. The worldwide gross now stands at Rs 119.50 cr.'The Paradise' earns Rs 15.25 cr on Day 3'The Paradise' began its theatrical run with Day 0 shows on September 23. The film collected Rs 11.60 cr from 900 shows that day. Its overall occupancy stood at 79.0%. The movie witnessed a major jump on its first official day. On September 24, it earned Rs 34.65 cr from 9,732 shows. The occupancy for the day was 49.3%.Its collection dropped to Rs 14.90 cr on Friday. The film had 7,049 shows and recorded 32.8% overall occupancy. Saturday brought a small increase, with the collection rising to Rs 15.25 cr. The film recorded 6,889 shows on Day 3. Its overall occupancy for the day stood at 33.4%.The Telugu version continued to dominate the language-wise figures on Day 3. It collected Rs 13.35 cr nett from 3,617 shows. The version recorded an occupancy of 46.1%. The Hindi version earned Rs 1.65 cr from 2,809 shows. Its overall occupancy stood at 19.0%.The Tamil version added Rs 25 lakhs from 463 shows. It recorded 21.0% occupancy. The three versions together contributed to the film's India net collection of Rs 76.40 cr after three days. The Telugu 2D version registered 43.00% overall occupancy on Saturday. Morning shows recorded 28.00%, while afternoon screenings reached 45.15%.Evening shows registered 45.38% occupancy. The night shows recorded the highest figure at 53.46%. The Hindi 2D version had an overall occupancy of 22.08%. Its morning shows recorded 10.55%, followed by 17.73% in the afternoon. Evening and night shows recorded 21.55% and 33.09%, respectively.The Tamil 2D version registered 30.39% overall occupancy. Its morning shows recorded 20.64%, while afternoon and evening shows stood at 14.36% and 11.18%. Night shows recorded 36.55%.Andhra Pradesh and Telangana contribute Rs 13.50 crThe state-wise gross figures show Andhra Pradesh and Telangana contributing the largest share on Day 3. The region recorded Rs 13.50 cr in gross collections.Karnataka added Rs 1.70 cr to the day's gross. Tamil Nadu contributed Rs 55 lakhs, while Kerala recorded Rs 10 lakhs. The rest of India contributed another Rs 2.15 cr. The combined gross collection across these regions stood at Rs 18.00 cr on Day 3.ETimes review discusses 'The Paradise' screenplayDirected by Srikanth Odela, 'The Paradise' features Nani and Kayadu Lohar in the lead roles.ETimes' review praised Srikanth Odela's approach to atmosphere and violence. It also discussed the screenplay and its handling of the characters and central conflict.The review reads, "Srikanth Odela clearly has a distinctive filmmaking voice, particularly in the way he creates atmosphere and stages violence. But visual confidence alone cannot compensate when the screenplay loses its grip on the characters and the central conflict. By the time the film reaches its final stretch, the exhaustion comes less from the darkness of the subject and more from how long the narrative keeps circling the same emotional territory."DISCLAIMER: The box office numbers and the data in this article are compiled from public and industry sources. In this testosterone-filled world, Keerthy Suresh and Jeeva Subramanian's warm performances provide the emotional anchor.Ilaiyaraaja's terrific music is a burst of thunder in the first half and a soft caress in the latter portions, lending the drama, and its delicate handling of queer lives and relationships, both weight and empathy."DISCLAIMER: The box office numbers and the data in this article are compiled from public and industry sources. articles.summary: Months after ‘Grey’s Anatomy’ star Eric Dane’s passing, his daughters are holding their father close to their hearts.
articles.body: Months after ‘Grey’s Anatomy’ star Eric Dane’s passing, his daughters are holding their father close to their hearts. In one of her recent appearances, Dane’s wife, Rebecca Gayheart, opened up about their life after his passing and how their daughters have been dealing with everything these days.Rebecca Gayheart opens up about how her daughters are doing after Eric Dane’s passingThe 55-year-old former actress and model recently attended the Step Up’s 2026 Annual Inspiration Awards. During a conversation with PEOPLE, Gayheart opened up about how their lives have been and how everything has changed in their household following Dane’s passing. She also shared that their daughters Billie Beatrice, 16, and Georgia Geraldine, 14, are ‘hanging’ on.She added during the interview: “You know, we’re hanging in there. I think it’s definitely a challenging season, but we’re doing our best. The girls are both in high school—which is also a big transition under any circumstance—so I’m just staying close to my kids."How Rebecca Gayheart deals with life when things get hardDuring the interview, she was also asked about how she deals with things sometimes when it all gets too much to handle. The ‘Beverly Hills’ star revealed that one of the main things that gets her through the hard times is spending time with people who love and care about her and those she can lean on.She mentioned, "friends. My children. Being under the same roof with my kids and having them next to me, safe, always makes me feel better. You know, there are certain people I like to talk to to get my feelings out, but really just—again—being connected to other human beings. That’s what gets me through.”About Rebecca Gayheart and Eric DaneRebecca Gayheart and Eric Dane met for the first time in 2003, and within 10 months of dating, the two decided to tie the knot in a private ceremony on October 29, 2004. While talking to Flaunt magazine in 2008, the actor briefly addressed how their relationship began, sharing, "It's probably one of the least interesting stories in the world. It went basically like this: 'You want to go out?' 'Yeah, sure.' Ten months later, we were married."In March 2010, Gayheart gave birth to the couple's first child, daughter Billie Beatrice. Earlier, as they prepared for parenthood, Dane featured on ‘The Ellen DeGeneres Show’ and opened up about how much he looked forward to becoming a father. "I'll be in the room. I'm going to stay close to my wife and make sure that she is all right. I'm really excited. I'm also very interested," he shared at the time. Their first daughter was named after Dane’s father. The couple later welcomed their second daughter, Georgia Geraldine, in December 2011.Eric Dane passed away in February 2026, almost a year after he announced that he had been diagnosed with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS).Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.body: Mohanlal's love for organic farming has given a unique character to his Elamakkara home in Ernakulam, Kochi. Away from film sets, the actor cultivates vegetables and other crops for his household.His home garden includes several vegetables commonly used in everyday cooking. Bitter gourd, tomatoes, lady's finger, long beans, green chilies and eggplants are grown organically on the premises.In a video shared by the actor in 2021, the garden also features lettuce, papaya, corn, bottle gourd and tapioca. Mohanlal has continued the cultivation for several years, making it a part of his routine at home.Mohanlal's home has a flourishing vegetable gardenMohanlal has maintained the organic garden beside his Elamakkara residence for years. His busy acting career has not stopped him from pursuing his interest in growing food. Lettuce, papaya, corn, bottle gourd and tapioca are also part of the cultivation.Actor revealed his farming routine during lockdownMohanlal introduced his fans to his organic farming activities during the 2021 lockdown. With people staying indoors, the actor used the period to showcase an activity he had already been pursuing.He shared a cinematic-style video from his home. Along with the video, Mohanlal wrote, "Organic Farming during lockdown at my home. Thanks to my Team behind the lockdown videos."Mohanlal had been growing vegetables for yearsIn the video, Mohanlal revealed that his farming efforts were not something he started during the lockdown. He said he had already been growing vegetables needed for his kitchen.At the time, the actor said he had been cultivating them for around four or five years. His garden therefore reflected an interest that developed well before the pandemic. Mohanlal's message also focused on making organic farming accessible to people with limited space. He pointed out that having a large yard is not essential to start growing vegetables.The actor suggested that people could use grow bags for cultivation. He also mentioned terraces as another option for those without enough space around their homes.A green corner away from his busy film lifeThe video also gave fans a glimpse of Mohanlal's Elamakkara residence. The house is surrounded by greenery and has a separate garden filled with flowering plants and shrubs. Although Mohanlal spends considerable time at his beachside residence in Chennai, he enjoys staying at his Elamakkara home when he is in Kerala.As reported by Moneytree Realty, Mohanlal's primary residence is a waterfront bungalow located in Thevara, Kochi.On the work front, Mohanlal was last seen in a cameo appearance in his daughter Vismaya Mohanlal's debut movie 'Thudakkam'. The film was directed by Jude Anthany Joseph. Mohanlal also appeared in a cameo role in Priyadarshan's 'Haiwaan'.DISCLAIMER: Figures presented in this article are derived from various public sources and are considered approximate unless explicitly noted. articles.title: Vishal suffers back injury during Purushan climax shoot in Goa: ‘I’m sorry I cannot attend the Nadigar Sangam general body meeting’
articles.summary: Actor Vishal revealed that he suffered a back injury while shooting an intense action sequence for his upcoming film ‘Purushan.’ The accident happened
articles.body: Actor Vishal revealed that he suffered a back injury while shooting an intense action sequence for his upcoming film ‘Purushan.’ The accident happened during the climax shoot in Goa, forcing the actor to take a break from his regular commitments. Vishal, who is also the General Secretary of the South Indian Artistes’ Association, confirmed he cannot attend the association’s upcoming general body meeting due to his injury. He also thanked everyone for recovery wishes and prayers.Vishal reveals details of ‘Purushan’ accidentSharing an update on social media, Vishal said the injury occurred during a demanding action sequence for ‘Purushan,’ directed by Sundar C. “The climax shoot of my next film, ‘Purushan’, directed by Sundar C, was happening in Goa. During an intense fight sequence, an unexpected accident occurred and I suffered an injury to my back,” Vishal said. The actor immediately underwent a medical examination following the incident and was advised to take complete rest before returning to his regular activities.Vishal to miss Nadigar Sangam general body meetingVishal also expressed disappointment over missing the Nadigar Sangam general body meeting because of the injury. “After the medical examination, the doctors advised me to take three weeks of rest to recover completely. I am extremely sorry that I will not be able to attend the Nadigar Sangam general body meeting taking place tomorrow,” he said. As the association’s General Secretary, Vishal has been involved in several of its activities, making his absence from the meeting particularly significant.Vishal thanks fans and well-wishers for their supportThe actor said he understood the importance of meeting members in person and apologised for being unable to attend. “I sincerely regret not being able to come in person and participate. I hope you will understand my situation. I am looking forward to recovering soon and returning to my regular activities,” Vishal said. He also thanked those who contacted him and expressed concern about his condition. “My heartfelt thanks to everyone who is praying for me and enquiring about my well-being with care,” he added.Vishal’s ‘Purushan’ shoot put on hold as he recoversThe injury comes while Vishal is working on ‘Purushan,’ his next collaboration with director Sundar C. The film’s climax action sequence appears to have been physically demanding, resulting in the accident that has forced the actor to take a three-week break.For now, Vishal’s focus will be on recovery before he returns to the sets and his association responsibilities. His latest statement also reassures fans that he is looking forward to getting back to his usual schedule once fully recovered.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Mamta Kulkarni returns to her 90s avatar, dances To ‘Koi Jaaye To Le Aaye’, viral video leaves internet saying ‘Yeh toh sanyasi ho gayi thi’
articles.summary: Mamta Kulkarni has once again become a talking point on social media, this time for a rather unexpected throwback to her Bollywood days.
articles.body: Mamta Kulkarni has once again become a talking point on social media, this time for a rather unexpected throwback to her Bollywood days. The actor, who stepped into a spiritual life after taking sanyas in 2025, was recently seen dancing to some of her best-known 1990s tracks at a film festival in Jaipur. The videos from the event have now gone viral, with many social media users reacting to the striking contrast between her current spiritual journey and her glamorous screen image from the 1990s.Mamta Kulkarni dances to her 90s songsThe actor was honoured with a Lifetime Achievement Award at the 14th Rajasthan Film Festival. During the celebrations, songs from her films played at the venue, prompting her to join students and dance on stage.She was seen dancing to popular tracks including ‘Koi Jaaye To Le Aaye’ from ‘Ghatak’, ‘Ek Munda Meri Umar Ka’ from ‘Karan Arjun’ and ‘Lamba Lamba Ghunghat’ from ‘Sabse Bada Khiladi’.While the performance brought back memories of her Bollywood era, her appearance became an equally discussed part of the videos. Mamta opted for a glamorous outfit for the occasion, which was notably different from the saffron-clad spiritual persona associated with her after she embraced sanyas.Social media reacts to her transformationThe viral clips prompted a range of reactions, particularly from users who remembered her as one of the prominent faces of 1990s Hindi cinema. Several comments pointed out the contrast between her former Bollywood image and her spiritual avatar.One user wrote, “Bhai ye to sanyashi ho gayi thi", while another commented, “Ye to sadhu ban gayi thi na."Others joked about her return to a glamorous appearance. One comment read, “Isne to sanyash le liya tha," while another said, “Are mahamandaleshwar." A user also quipped, “From moksh to maya reverse concept."At the same time, many people focused on her appearance and praised her for looking glamorous. One user wrote, “She looks amazing," while another called her “My generation ka super star."Another person defended her decision to appear glamorous, writing, “Isko sadhvi nahi banana tha. She is very glamorous and gorgeous."Mamta's spiritual journey began at Maha KumbhMamta embraced sanyas during the Maha Kumbh in Prayagraj on January 24, 2025. She performed the Pind Daan ritual at the Sangam and was given the spiritual name Shri Yamai Mamta Nand Giri. She was subsequently appointed Mahamandaleshwar of the Kinnar Akhara.Her association with the position later became controversial. She announced her resignation in February 2025, although she subsequently said that the resignation had not been accepted and that she would continue pursuing her spiritual path.The actor had stayed away from Mumbai for nearly 24 years before returning to the city in December 2024. During her years away from the film industry, her name was linked to Vicky Goswami, who has been described in media reports as an alleged drug lord.In 2016, Thane Police named Mamta as an accused in a drug case connected to Goswami and alleged that she had attended a meeting in Kenya related to the racket. She denied involvement in the drug trade.A significant legal development came in 2024 when the Bombay High Court quashed the case against her, observing that the proceedings were manifestly frivolous and that there was insufficient material to continue the prosecution.She had earlier ruled Bollywood in the 90sMamta's recent appearance has also reminded fans of the career that made her a familiar face in Hindi cinema. She featured in several popular films during the 1990s, including ‘Tirangaa’, ‘Aashiq Aawara’, ‘Waqt Hamara Hai’, ‘Krantiveer’, ‘Karan Arjun’, ‘Sabse Bada Khiladi’, ‘Ghatak’ and ‘China Gate’.She won the Filmfare Lux New Face of the Year award for ‘Aashiq Aawara’ in 1994. After years away from Mumbai, her return in 2024 generated considerable interest, although she had said at the time that she was not planning a return to Bollywood and that her focus remained on her spiritual journey.Her latest dance videos, however, have given fans an unexpected glimpse of the actor reconnecting with the music and films that defined a significant chapter of her career.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Mammootty's tilak at National Awards draws criticism; Harisree Yousuf reacts, 'Religion is meant to make human beings better'
articles.summary: Malayalam actor - comedian Harisree Yousuf responded to a derogatory comment directed at the National Award-winning actor Mammootty.
articles.body: Malayalam actor - comedian Harisree Yousuf responded to a derogatory comment directed at the National Award-winning actor Mammootty. Harisree Yousuf was reacting to a video showing Mammootty being welcomed in Gujarat with a tilak on his forehead.Mammootty had travelled to Gujarat to receive the National Award. A video from his visit showed him being greeted with the traditional welcome gesture. The footage also prompted a comment criticising the actor for accepting the tilak.Harisree Yousuf addressed the comment and spoke about religion, faith and how people respond to cultural practices.Harisree Yousuf responds to Mammootty commentIn his Facebook video, Harisree Yousuf said Malayalis were proud of Mammootty after his National Award win. He questioned the criticism aimed at the actor over the tilak shown in the video.The actor said, “Malayalis were all very happy that he received the National Award for Best Actor. We applauded for him. But one person posted a comment against him. The person who posted this comment is someone named Abbas.When Mammootty went to receive the award, a tilak was applied to his forehead. He bent down to have the tilak applied. This person felt that it was a huge offence. Son, you are like a frog in a well. Mammootty is an artist. I am also a small-time artist. We artists do not have narrow-minded thinking. We think a little more broadly. So, people like you, who carry only 'religion' in their minds, will think like this.'Whether you apply a tilak' or prayHarisree Yousuf then spoke about the similarities between different forms of religious expression. He said that applying a tilak, making the sign of the cross or offering Muslim prayers all represent devotion to God.He said, "Have you heard the song that says, ‘Whether you apply a tilak, make the sign of the cross or bow down and pray, the one who sees is the same, the one who listens is the same, the merciful God’?” Haven’t you heard that song? Whether you make the sign of the cross, apply a tilak or bow down and pray, everything is directed towards God. It shows love for our Creator."He compares the welcome to a hotel receptionHarisree Yousuf also offered an explanation for the welcome Mammootty received. He compared the gesture to the way guests are traditionally welcomed at certain hotels."Son, when you go to a big hotel, this is one of the ways they welcome guests. When guests arrive, they give them a bouquet and apply a tilak on their forehead before welcoming them inside."Harisree Yousuf speaks about religion and charityHarisree Yousuf pointed to Mammootty's achievements and the respect he commands among Malayalis.He said, "You abused a person who is respected and admired by Malayalis across the world, a person with so much talent and so many achievements who has brought recognition to our state, and who has won the National Award four times.Abbas, look at the good things that person does for our society. The organisations he supports as a patron conduct so many charitable activities here. He has helped provide free heart surgeries to so many children. Can you ever do at least one thing that benefits this society? No."He also spoke about the purpose of religion and criticised the use of religious identity to attack others.Continuing his response, Harisree Yousuf said religion should encourage people to become better human beings rather than create divisions."People like you can come to comment sections, abuse someone's father, hurl insults, and then bring God into it and invoke religion. That is all you can do. Religion is necessary, but what is religion for? It is not for human beings to fight with each other. Religion is meant to make human beings better."Harisree Yousuf also criticised what he described as communal thinking and asked the commenter not to repeat such remarks."Abbas, the country that best suits your way of thinking is Taliban. That is where your mentality belongs. I am not telling you to go there. Because if you go there, they won't let you in.""You have to live in India itself because you were born and raised in India. I am not foolish enough to tell you to leave this country. I am only saying that based on your nature and way of thinking. Son, this is the great nation of India. In reality, it is people who think like you who create communalism here. Don't do anything like this again.”Who is Harisree Yousuf?For the unversed, Harisree Yousuf is an actor who has appeared in several Malayalam movies and stage shows. His filmography includes movies such as 'Meow', 'Ini Utharam' and 'Amar Akbar Anthony'.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Dani García, chef: "La mejor forma de dar la vuelta a la tortilla es calentar las dos sartenes a la vez"
articles.standfirst: El cocinero malagueño utiliza una sartén doble y calienta sus dos partes para evitar que la tortilla pierda temperatura al darle la vuelta
articles.summary: El cocinero malagueño utiliza una sartén doble y calienta sus dos partes para evitar que la tortilla pierda temperatura al darle la vuelta
articles.body: Dar la vuelta a una tortilla de patata es uno de los momentos más delicados de una receta que, sobre el papel, parece sencilla. El plato puede estar perfectamente preparado y, sin embargo, todo puede complicarse en cuestión de segundos al intentar voltearlo. Dani García tiene un sistema para evitarlo y no consiste en utilizar el tradicional plato: el chef utiliza una sartén doble y calienta las dos partes antes de darle la vuelta. El cocinero malagueño mostró su método al preparar la tortilla de patata que sirve en Tragabuches. La clave está en utilizar dos sartenes del mismo tamaño que pueden unirse y funcionar como una sola. De esta manera, cuando llega el momento de voltear la tortilla, la segunda sartén ya está caliente y preparada para continuar la cocción. La técnica tiene una ventaja importante frente al sistema tradicional de utilizar un plato. Al pasar la tortilla de una sartén caliente a otra que está a temperatura ambiente, se produciría una pérdida de calor. Dani García busca evitar precisamente ese cambio. El sistema parte de una sartén doble específica para tortillas. Son dos recipientes idénticos que se pueden acoplar mediante una unión que funciona como bisagra. Algunas incorporan además un borde que permite cerrarlas evitando que el contenido se salga y mangos que facilitan sujetarlas durante el volteo. Para preparar la tortilla, García pone las dos partes a calentar simultáneamente, aunque una de ellas a una temperatura algo inferior porque será la que utilice para terminar de cuajar el segundo lado. Cuando la primera sartén está caliente, incorpora la mezcla de patata y huevo. Una vez que la tortilla ha comenzado a cuajarse por los bordes, engrasa la segunda sartén, también caliente, con un poco de mantequilla. Después acopla ambas partes, les da la vuelta y retira la primera sartén. La tortilla continúa entonces cocinándose en la segunda, que ya estaba caliente. El objetivo es conseguir que la tortilla mantenga una temperatura de cocción estable durante todo el proceso y, al mismo tiempo, reducir el riesgo de que termine en el suelo o partida sobre la cocina, uno de los accidentes domésticos más habituales cuando se utiliza el método tradicional. El sistema para darle la vuelta es solo una parte de la receta del chef. García utiliza 1,2 kilos de patatas y nueve huevos para elaborar su tortilla, además de aceite de oliva virgen extra, sal y mantequilla. Es, además, un cocinero que se declara contrario a añadir cebolla a la tortilla. Las patatas se cortan en rodajas finas, de entre 2 y 3 milímetros, y se fríen a unos 180 grados. Mientras tanto, el chef bate los huevos con un chorrito de aceite de oliva virgen extra hasta conseguir una mezcla cremosa. Una vez fritas, las patatas pasan directamente al huevo y se dejan reposar para que absorban parte de la mezcla. Después se procede a cuajar la tortilla utilizando las dos partes de la sartén doble.

articles.title: Santi, vecino de Madrid: "Pago 1.000 euros al mes y quieren echarme porque tienen otro modelo de negocio"
articles.standfirst: Santi asegura que lleva 17 años pagando 1.000 euros al mes por su vivienda y denuncia la situación que viven 30 familias de su edificio
articles.summary: Santi asegura que lleva 17 años pagando 1.000 euros al mes por su vivienda y denuncia la situación que viven 30 familias de su edificio
articles.body: Santi es uno de los vecinos que se han concentrado en Madrid para protestar por la situación de la vivienda y por el riesgo de perder sus casas. En una entrevista realizada por 'Malas Lenguas' durante la acampada en la Puerta del Sol, explica que lleva 17 años viviendo en su domicilio y pagando 1.000 euros al mes, pero que sus caseros quieren que abandone la vivienda. "Yo me tenía que haber marchado, pero tengo que decir que llevo 17 años pagando 1.000 euros al mes y resulta que quieren más", explica durante la entrevista. Según su testimonio, el conflicto se prolonga desde hace dos años, periodo durante el que los vecinos han intentado negociar para poder permanecer en sus viviendas. Santi también denuncia durante la entrevista el estado del edificio en el que reside. Según asegura, existen problemas de mantenimiento y el ascensor permanece averiado. En este contexto recuerda a una vecina de 80 años, María Luisa, que, según relata, padecía cáncer y murió en su vivienda porque no podía bajar a la calle. "Esta es la gente de la que estamos hablando. Solo quieren dinero", afirma. El vecino asegura que la situación afecta a 30 familias del edificio. Explica que los residentes llegaron a firmar una carta, junto al Sindicato de Inquilinas, para intentar negociar su permanencia. Sin embargo, sostiene que no han encontrado disposición por parte de la propiedad: "No nos quieren, tienen otro modelo de negocio", afirma. Preguntado por cómo son esas negociaciones, Santi responde que para él es "como si hablases con una pared". Según cuenta, la comunicación con los vecinos se habría producido a través de personas que se presentan como negociadores y que, en algunos casos, habrían ofrecido 10.000 euros a cambio de abandonar la vivienda. También denuncia lo que considera una situación de deterioro de los pisos que quedan vacíos. "Clausurando el piso que se queda vacío, le ponen una puerta antiokupas, pero es que lo clausuran con basura adentro", relata. También menciona la existencia de goteras. Ante la pregunta de cómo afronta psicológicamente llevar dos años sabiendo que quieren que abandone su casa, Santi responde con seguridad: "Yo duermo muy bien, porque vamos a ganar". Cuando el periodista le pregunta si lo tiene claro, responde: "Yo lo tengo muy claro". El vecino explica que acudió a la concentración de la Puerta del Sol y que, aunque inicialmente había acudido para participar en la manifestación, no descartaba quedarse a dormir durante la acampada.

articles.summary: The fallout from Saturday’s Turn 1 chaos at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix has officially escalated from a standard paddock squabble into a full-blown internation...
articles.body:
The fallout from Saturday's Turn 1 chaos at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix has officially escalated from a standard paddock squabble into a full-blown international diplomatic incident.

After McLaren's Lando Norris demanded a one-race ban for Alpine rookie Franco Colapinto following their multi-car pile-up, the entire nation of Argentina seemingly took it personally. Now, high-ranking government officials are entering the F1 chat to defend their driver.

On Sunday, Pablo Quirno—Argentina's Minister of Foreign Affairs— took to X (formerly Twitter) to publicly call out what he sees as glaring hypocrisy from the reigning World Champion.

Quirno posted a sarcastic response to Norris's demands, offering an absolute masterclass in political trolling.

"Sure, Lando Norris called for a penalty for the driver who crashed into Oscar Piastri in Montreal 2025," Quirno wrote before delivering the deadpan punchline: "Ah, no… right".

To ensure the message hit home, Quirno attached a brutal piece of photographic evidence to his post.

The image highlights the infamous 2025 Canadian Grand Prix collision, showing a papaya-on-papaya disaster where Norris lost control and plowed directly into the side of his own McLaren teammate, Oscar Piastri , pinning him violently against the concrete barriers.

Quirno's implication is crystal clear: when Norris made a massive, race-ending misjudgment that wiped out a competitor (and his own teammate, no less), the British driver certainly wasn't marching into the media pen demanding a self-imposed race ban.

BAKU, AZERBAIJAN – SEPTEMBER 25: Fifth placed qualifier Lando Norris of Great Britain and McLaren arrives in parc ferme during qualifying ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of Azerbaijan at Baku City Circuit on September 25, 2026 in Baku, Azerbaijan. (Photo by Sam Bloxham/LAT Images)

Colapinto's late-braking lock-up in Baku was undeniably a costly rookie error, especially given the tight championship margins. However, when a driver starts demanding the most severe penalty in motorsport for a botched Safety Car restart, they need to ensure their own crash history is entirely spotless.

With George Russell and Max Verstappen already publicly dismissing Norris's demands as unnecessarily harsh, and the Argentine government now dropping photo evidence of his past mistakes, the McLaren driver is finding out the hard way that throwing stones from a glass cockpit rarely ends well.

articles.title: Why do some Indian villages still cook food underground? The centuries-old cooking technique that turns pits into natural ovens.
articles.summary: Discover the ancient culinary technique of pit cooking in Indian villages, where food is prepared underground to enhance flavors and foster community gatherings. This centuries-old tradition connects generations and showcases India's diverse cultural heritage.
articles.body: Over centuries, food has become much more than just a mode of survival. It carries within it years of trials, practice and experimentation. These practices are not only a response to our physical needs but a tapestry of culture, availability and adaptation. More than that, they also carry generations of stories. One such practice is the art of pit cooking, spanning cultures, traditions and even ingredients. Going beyond the increasingly popular concept of fast and readily available foods, pit cooking teaches us the importance of patience. Slow-cooked meat and vegetables in an earthen pit, trapping the woody and smoky flavour into their meaty fibres, give off a mesmerising aroma while also teaching us the art of anticipation.The essence of pit cookingGoing back hundreds of years, pit cooking is one of the oldest culinary methods of cooking food. Almost every community has developed some dish cooked within an earthen pit. Also known as earth-oven cooking, the ancient technique involves cooking meat and vegetables in an earthen pit heated with stones, wood, charcoal or cow-dung cakes, which are used widely by Indian communities. The earth’s natural insulation creates an environment where the food is slowly cooked, infusing it with a distinct earthy flavour. This is what readily distinguishes it from other methods of cooking.Pit cooking in IndiaIndia, the hub for integrated cooking practices perfected through its millennia-old culinary tradition. Pit cooking was deeply infused within the cooking customs of India. Dating back to ancient times, when fire rituals required certain offerings of food to be cooked within earthen pits, communities in India still follow similar culinary practices. The ingredients have changed over time, integrating influences from all the communities that had a relation with them: Persian, Portuguese, Arab and others.India has many versions of pit cooking. In recent times, one of the most fascinating pit-cooking traditions comes from the pit masters of Rajasthan: Khad Khargosh, where game rabbit or other royally hunted animals were cooked underground with only limited spices. Hyderabad’s famous Dum Biryani is cooked by burying the handi underground. Similarly, Lucknow’s Zamin Doz, inspired by the Persians, is cooked in sealed pots in pits. Whether it’s Goa’s meaty pit seafood or Gujarat’s vegetarian Umbadyu, pit cooking transcends all boundaries.A method shaped by its surroundingsFor communities that practised it, pit cooking was also a practical response to their surroundings. Before modern ovens, gas stoves and specialised cookware, the earth itself could become a cooking vessel. Stones, clay, wood, leaves and cow-dung cakes were materials that could be gathered locally and used to create a functioning oven. Thus, the technique not only represents culinary experimentation, but also how communities adapted their food practices to the resources available to them.Pit cooking demanded patience and community too. It might take several hours to prepare the pit, build the fire, heat the stones and finally uncover the food. It turned cooking from a quick household chore into a communal activity, especially at festivals, parties and big get-togethers. This turned cooking into a community event. People gathered together, brought in ingredients and had a delicious meal afterwards. These habits held together families and even cultures.A tradition that refuses to disappearModern kitchens have made cooking considerably faster, but pit cooking survives precisely because it offers something speed cannot easily reproduce. The slow accumulation of heat, the smoky aroma and the anticipation of uncovering food from beneath the earth are part of the experience itself.For some communities, therefore, pit cooking is more than an old culinary technique. It is a reminder of how earlier generations understood fire, food and their environment. The pit becomes an oven, the earth becomes insulation, and the cooking process becomes a story passed from one generation to another. It connects them with the earth and nature, as everything that is used is taken directly from it.Stories and traditions were created through the act of gathering, contributing, cooking and enjoying the meal, which crossed the boundaries of caste, creed and even generations, allowing everyone to come around the pit and share a timeless bond.You use AI every day. articles.title: Suniel Shetty recalls his childhood obsession with cricket, reveals he has been following Rohit Sharma since he was 16
articles.summary: Actor Suniel Shetty discusses his childhood obsession with cricket and his admiration for Indian cricketer Rohit Sharma during an episode of 'Family Full House with Rohit Sharma'.
articles.body: Actor Suniel Shetty opened up about his deep love for cricket and his long-standing admiration for Indian cricketer Rohit Sharma.During his appearance on 'Family Full House with Rohit Sharma,' the 'Hera Pheri' actor recalled his passion for the sport and said he has been an avid cricket fan for years and would even go out of his way to watch footage of pace bowlers at a time when cricket matches were not easily available on television. Talking about his love for cricket, Suniel Shetty said, "Main kitna bada cricket buff hoon woh duniya jaanti hai. Shayad jitna inhone cricket nahi khela hoga, utna maine khayalon mein khela hai. Pehle zamaane mein television pe aate nahi the, toh pace bowlers ko dekhne Indo-American Society jaata tha, aur unke rushes dekhne ke liye, unki clippings dekhne ke liye." ("I am known to be a huge cricket buff. Perhaps I have played more cricket in my imagination than they have actually played. In those days, cricket matches were not shown much on television, so I would go to the Indo-American Society to watch pace bowlers and see their footage and clippings.")The 'Dhadkan' actor also recalled how Sir Viv Richards has always been his favourite cricketer and how he started following Rohit when rohit was just 16. He shared, "Mere hamesha favourite cricketer rahe the aur aaj bhi mere favourite hi hain Sir Viv Richards. Aur main Rohit ko shayad jab se woh 16-17 saal ka tha, tab se follow karta aa raha hoon. Dr. PV Shetty Rohit ke baare mein hamesha baat karte the. Main hamesha dekhne jaata tha, baat karta tha. Chhota sa Rohit, but same hi game, same amount of time." ("My favourite cricketer has always been Sir Viv Richards, and he remains my favourite even today. I have been following Rohit since he was around 16 or 17 years old. Dr. PV Shetty would often talk about Rohit, and I would always go to watch him and speak to him. He was a young Rohit back then, but the game was the same, and he spent the same amount of time playing.")For Suniel, the resemblance went beyond Rohit's cricket. Drawing a comparison between the two, He added, "Toh main uss waqt bhi bolta tha ki agar Sir Viv Richards ki koi mujhe yaad dilata hai, it's Rohit Sharma. Same swag, woh Caribbean swag, yeh Desi swag."( "Even then, I used to say that if anyone reminded me of Sir Viv Richards, it was Rohit Sharma. The same swag - that Caribbean swag in him, and this desi swag in Rohit.")Furthermore, Rohit recalled his first memorable meeting with Suniel when he was around 16 and playing for Indian Oil. "Mujhe abhi bhi yaad hai jo Suniel sir ne bataya ki main 16 saal ka tha aur main apni company ke liye khel raha tha, Indian Oil ke liye. Yeh match Bandra Kurla Complex main ground mein ho raha tha, aur main bas pad up karke baitha tha, batting ke liye jaane ke liye. Tabhi mujhe pata chala ki sir wahan par aane wale hain. Toh maine bola, yeh kaunsa match hai? Yahan pe kyun aayenge? But yeh hai inka, jo abhi inhone bataya ki inhone mere se zyada apne khayalon mein khela hai. But inka jo pyaar hai cricket ke liye, hum sab jaante hain." ("I still remember what Suniel sir mentioned. I was 16 and playing for my company, Indian Oil. The match was taking place at a ground in Bandra Kurla Complex, and I was just padded up, waiting to go in to bat. That's when I found out that sir was going to be there. I thought, 'What kind of match is this? Why would he come here?' But that's him. As he just mentioned, he has probably played more cricket in his imagination than I have. But we all know how much he loves cricket.")Rohit also remembers Suniel meeting his mentor PV Shetty during a match and being completely engrossed in the game. He shared, "Aur tab mujhe realise hua ki inhone abhi bataya ki itna cricket dekha hai inhone, aur khelte bhi the. Under-19 khela hai inhone. Jab main baitha tha aur Suniel sir aake baithe PV Shetty ke saath, jo mere mentor the. Unhone mujhe kaafi help ki mere younger days mein. Unhone mujhe bola ki, 'Aapko inse milna chahiye, yeh bahut cricket pasand karte hain.' Main bola, of course kaun nahi milna chahta. Lekin main dekh raha tha inko side se hi ki kar kya rahe hain yeh. Par inka dhyaan poora cricket pe tha ki yeh kitna accha shot khel raha hai." ("And that's when I realized that, as he just mentioned, he has watched a lot of cricket and has also played the game. He played Under-19 cricket. I was sitting there when Suniel sir came and sat with PV Shetty, who was my mentor and helped me a lot during my younger days. He told me, 'You should meet him, he really loves cricket.' I thought, of course, who wouldn't want to meet him? But I was watching him from the side to see what he was doing. His entire attention, however, was on the cricket and on how well someone was playing a shot.")On a related note, the "Family Full House with Rohit Sharma" airs every Saturday and Sunday on Sony Entertainment Television and Sony LIV.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Poonam Dhillon recalls Lata Mangeshkar's legacy: 'Without her, Hindi film music would have been incomplete'
articles.summary: Actress Poonam Dhillon honors the legacy of Lata Mangeshkar during a tribute event at Tagore Theatre, celebrating her unparalleled impact on Hindi cinema and music.
articles.body: Actress Poonam Dhillon remembered legendary playback singer Lata Mangeshkar and her unparalleled contribution to Hindi cinema.Speaking to IANS while attending 'Surila Safar-30: An Evening of Bollywood Melodies' at Tagore Theatre, she recalling her early days in the film industry. Poonam said Lata Mangeshkar had lent her voice to songs in almost all the films she had worked in during her career."Lata ji is very dear to all of us. Without her, the music of Hindi films would have been incomplete. It is a great thing that she is being honoured and remembered here. And that too in my lovely Tagore Theatre. It is a great joy for me," Poonam said.The actress also shared a personal connection with the iconic theatre, recalling how she had been visiting the venue for concerts since her childhood."We used to come here for our concerts since childhood. It is a very special day for me," she added.Poonam, who has worked in hundreds of films, further recalled the lasting impact of Lata Mangeshkar's voice on her cinematic journey."I have done hundreds of films. Except for one or two films, she has sung in all of them. All of her songs are one of the best. They are very beautiful songs," she said.The evening celebrated the timeless melodies of Bollywood and paid tribute to the enduring legacy of Lata Mangeshkar.For the unversed, legendary playback singer Lata Mangeshkar, fondly known as the 'Nightingale of India' and 'Swar Kokila,' passed away on February 6, 2022, at the age of 92. She died at Mumbai's Breach Candy Hospital following multiple organ failure after testing positive for COVID-19.Her death marked the end of an era in Indian music and prompted an outpouring of grief and tributes from across the country, including from Prime Minister Narendra Modi and several other political leaders and celebrities.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.body: Years before Vinod Khanna became one of Bollywood’s most respected veteran actors, his career took an unexpected turn when he walked away from films at the height of his stardom to follow spiritual guru Osho Rajneesh. After spending nearly five years away from the film industry, Khanna eventually returned to the big screen, and his comeback became one of the talking points in Bollywood at the time.Among the films he took up after his return was Mahesh Bhatt’s ‘Prem Dharm’, which paired him with Dimple Kapadia. Looking back at the making of the film, an old incident involving an intimate scene between the two actors has often been recalled in reports over the years.The intimate scene that reportedly went beyond the director’s cueAccording to reports by News24, Vinod and Dimple were filming a sequence that involved an embrace followed by a kiss. The scene reportedly took an unexpected turn when Mahesh Bhatt called “cut”, but Khanna allegedly continued for a few moments.Different versions of the incident have surfaced over the years. Some accounts claimed that the actor may not have heard the director’s instruction, while others suggested that he became too immersed in the scene after returning to such sequences following his long absence from cinema.Reports further claimed that Bhatt and members of the crew eventually stepped in to stop the sequence.Dimple Kapadia was reportedly left shakenThe incident was said to have left Dimple Kapadia shocked and uncomfortable. According to the accounts, she immediately went to her make-up room after the scene ended.Bhatt reportedly later spoke to Khanna about what had happened and advised him to talk to Dimple, explain the situation and apologise. Some versions of the story also claimed that Khanna acknowledged that he had lost control while performing the scene.However, the exact circumstances have remained unclear, with different retellings offering different explanations for why the actor allegedly continued after the director had called “cut”.Vinod Khanna’s unusual Bollywood comebackThe incident took place during a particularly significant phase of Khanna’s career. Before stepping away from films, he had established himself as one of Hindi cinema’s leading stars. His decision to leave the industry for a spiritual journey with Osho had therefore come as a major surprise.His eventual return after nearly five years generated considerable curiosity among audiences and filmmakers. ‘Prem Dharm’ was among the projects that marked this new chapter, with Khanna once again taking on film roles after spending years away from the sets.The reported incident from the film has continued to surface in retrospectives about Khanna’s career, particularly because it came soon after his return to Bollywood. While accounts of what exactly happened during that shoot have differed, the episode remains part of the many stories surrounding the actor’s unusual journey from Bollywood stardom to spiritual life and back to the film industry.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Sarah Santaolalla, sobre la crisis de la vivienda: “Nadie está poniendo en el foco a un señor que vive en Madrid y tiene una segunda casa en Benidorm”
articles.standfirst: La analista política ha hablado en ‘Malas lenguas’, de TVE
articles.summary: La analista política ha hablado en ‘Malas lenguas’, de TVE
articles.body: La crisis de la vivienda vive un punto álgido en nuestro país, sobre todo a raíz del desahucio de Maricarmen, una vecina de 87 años expulsada de la vivienda en la que había residido durante siete décadas. El asunto está presente en las tertulias políticas de todos los programas de televisión, incluido, por supuesto, ‘Malas lenguas’, donde Sarah Santaolalla ha hablado sobre ello. “Está hablando del pequeño propietario para tocar esa empatía para los espectadores que nos están viendo. Nadie está poniendo en el foco a un señor que vive en Madrid y tiene una segunda casa en Benidorm o en Marbella o donde la tenga y pasa allí los veranos”, afirma la analista política tajante. “Se estableció, tanto en los decretos como en las leyes, cómo eran los grandes propietarios. Y era a partir de cinco casas. Si tienes más de cinco casas, ¿te parece que todavía eres una víctima del sistema? No, no, es que cuando se habla de pequeño propietario, el pequeño propietario no es el fondo buitre del que se está hablando”, proseguía. Dicho esto, la colaboradora ha dejado claro que “una persona que está pagando una hipoteca porque tiene alquilada otra casa no es el problema de la vivienda”. “Lo que no está seguro es la gente que está viviendo en una casa que está pagando hoy un alquiler de 1.000 euros y que mañana puede venir su casero y decirle que paga 2.000 o se va a la puñetera calle”, ha sentenciado. “Esa es la gente que no está segura. Y esa es para la gente que hay que legislar. Y para eso es importante intervenir en el mercado y tomar medidas valientes, no solo pequeños propietarios”, concluía Sarah Santaolalla, en un día donde se ha producido la acampada en la Puerta del Sol como señal de protesta ante este asunto.

articles.title: Motivational quote of the day by MrBeast: ‘You just keep doing something; you'll get better at it,’ a powerful life lesson on hard work and consistency from the beloved YouTuber
articles.summary: Explore MrBeast's powerful motivational quote that emphasizes the importance of hard work, consistency, and self-improvement in achieving success. Learn from his journey and insights shared on 'The Joe Rogan Experience.'
articles.body: Getting good at something usually takes a lot longer than people see from the outside. The final result might look easy, but there are usually plenty of bad attempts, mistakes and things that did not work before getting there.MrBeast, whose real name is Jimmy Donaldson, has built his entire career around that idea. He started making YouTube videos as a teenager, long before anyone knew his name. Over the years, Jimmy kept trying different ideas, figuring out what clicked with viewers and what simply did not work. That trial-and-error eventually helped turn him into one of the biggest creators on the platform.Jimmy talked about that journey during his interview on 'The Joe Rogan Experience.' While discussing how people can turn an idea or skill into a career, he explained why simply continuing to work at something matters.Today’s motivational quote of the day by MrBeast reads: “You just keep doing something; you'll get better at it. Be objective, be self-analytical, like recognise what you're doing wrong and what you're doing right and get better at it and constantly try to improve.”What does the quote by MrBeast mean?He is not saying that simply repeating the same thing over and over will automatically make you successful. You have to pay attention to what you are doing.What went wrong? What worked? What could have been done differently? Then you try again.That has been a major part of how Jimmy approached YouTube. His videos did not become huge overnight. He spent years making videos, studying the platform and trying to understand what made people click and keep watching.How is the quote by MrBeast relevant today?It is very easy to look at someone's success and forget how much practice came before it. A creator has millions of followers now, so people assume they must have always known exactly what they were doing. A successful writer makes a great article, so nobody sees the dozens of average pieces that came before it. The same thing happens with almost anything. You get better by actually doing it.If you want to write, write. If you want to make videos, make videos. If you want to start a business, start learning how one works. The first attempt probably will not be your best one, and that is fine. The useful part is being honest enough to look at your work afterwards. That is where improvement happens.Early life of MrBeastJimmy Donaldson was born on May 7, 1998, in Wichita, Kansas, and grew up in North Carolina. He became interested in YouTube when he was still a teenager and started uploading videos under the name MrBeast.His early videos were nowhere near the scale of the productions he is known for today. According to the official MrBeast website, he spent years experimenting with gaming videos, commentary and different types of content before finding a formula that worked.One of his early major breakthroughs came in 2017 with a video of himself counting to 100,000. The video took around 40 hours to make and became his first major viral hit, according to his official biography.How did MrBeast rise to fame?MrBeast's YouTube channel grew as he became known for increasingly ambitious videos, challenges, giveaways and large-scale productions.Instead of treating each successful video as the end goal, he kept putting what he learned and earned back into the next project. His official website describes this cycle as a key part of how the MrBeast brand grew.That approach eventually took him beyond YouTube too, with businesses and projects including Beast Philanthropy, Feastables and the competition series 'Beast Games'. But underneath all of that is the same idea Jimmy discussed with Joe Rogan. Keep doing the work. Look at what you did. Figure out what needs fixing. Then do it again.There is no guarantee that every attempt will work. But if you keep learning from each one, you are not really starting from zero the next time. And that may be the most useful part of MrBeast's advice: you do not have to be great at something when you begin. You just have to keep getting better.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. Download the TOI app.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: 'What is the point of UNPLEASANT ANTi SMOKING REELS?': Sanjay Gupta slams smoking posters of ‘Animal’, ‘Dhurandhar’, ‘Love & War’
articles.summary: Filmmaker Sanjay Gupta has raised questions about why Bollywood continues to associate smoking with a leading man's image, particularly on posters.
articles.body: Filmmaker Sanjay Gupta has raised questions about why Bollywood continues to associate smoking with a leading man's image, particularly on posters. On Sunday, the director shared posters of Ranbir Kapoor from Sandeep Reddy Vanga's ‘Animal’, Ranveer Singh from Aditya Dhar's ‘Dhurandhar’, and Vicky Kaushal from Sanjay Leela Bhansali's ‘Love & War’, pointing out that all three actors were depicted smoking in their looks.Sanjay Gupta questions Bollywood's smoking postersTaking to X (formerly Twitter) on Sunday, Sanjay shared a collage featuring the three actors, questioning the contradiction between the anti-smoking disclaimers shown in theatres and the smoking imagery used on film posters. He wrote, "What is the point of those unpleasant anti smoking reels we have to endure before and during films when these are the posters of the films?".Users bring up Gupta's own film ‘Kaante’The post soon sparked a debate in the comments section, with one user pointing to Gupta's own 2002 film Kaante, referencing a song that mentions smoking. The user wrote, "Suprised that this is coming from the director of the movie Kaante which has a song which says 'ciggrate ke dhuan ka challa banake, collar ko thodasa upar chada ke'...what an irony." Gupta hit back directly, noting that the norms around smoking-related messaging were different back then. He wrote, "There were no non smoking ads then you genius."Other users react to the debateThe discussion drew several other users who echoed Gupta's larger point about the portrayal of smoking in films. Drawing a parallel to disclaimers on streaming platforms, one user wrote, "It's a joke, it's like watching a show on Netflix and apple and being warned about alcohol consumption." Another user took issue with how Indian cinema repeatedly links cigarettes with masculinity, commenting, "Because these people think that cigarette is the only thing that shows a man masculine. This is the lack of creativity. All Indian film industries are suffering from 'masculinity sycophancy'. Bhaad mai gaya content, story aur creativity." Someone else voiced their agreement, writing, "Couldn't agree more, dead right."CBFC tightens rules on substance depictionThis development comes as regulations around depicting substance use in films are being made stricter. The CBFC has put out a fresh set of guidelines outlining what content is permissible on screen and how sensitive topics must be approached. These rules, notified under the Cinematograph Act by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting on September 16, require films featuring narcotics to carry mandatory anti-drug warnings, while continuing to uphold restrictions on violence, sensitive subject matter and anything that could strain India's diplomatic relations. This move accompanies the Centre's decision to reconstitute the CBFC, bringing in a new 18-member board.Mandatory anti-drug warning for filmsAmong the most significant changes is the requirement for films depicting the consumption, use or trafficking of narcotic drugs or psychotropic substances to carry a mandatory on-screen warning. Such scenes will now need to display the message: "Illicit Narcotics Destroy Health and Guarantees Imprisonment. Say No to Drugs."New CBFC board announcedThe updated certification rules came alongside the Centre's announcement of a new CBFC board. The 18-member panel brings together actors Preity Zinta, Pankaj Tripathi, Suniel Shetty, Pallavi Joshi and Prosenjit Chatterjee, filmmaker Priyadarshan and Grammy-winning musician Ricky Kej, with Shashi Shekhar Vempati continuing in his role as CBFC chairperson. Other members include filmmaker Neela Madhab Panda, actor Manoj Joshi, singer and former parliamentarian Hans Raj Hans, producer Supriya Yarlagadda, poet Yatindra Mishra, actors Roopali Ganguly and Nishigandha Wad, theatre director Waman Kendre and writer Ramesh Patange.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Southsea traders blame Victorious Festival for revenue losses
articles.summary: Some Portsmouth traders have criticised the impact of Victorious Festival, held on Southsea Common.
articles.body:
Businesses in Portsmouth have raised concerns over the impact of an annual music festival, with one claiming it has lost almost £1m in revenue over the past decade.

Portsmouth City Council heard from local traders during a meeting considering whether to agree new contracts with Victorious Festival and the Great South Run.

Speaking to councillors, Jimmy Norman, director of Clarence Pier, said the authority should "address the impact" of Victorious but said he did not want to see it leave the city.

James Ralls, managing director and co-founder of Victorious Festival, said organisers "try to work with every business".

Norman said that over the past 10 years the pier had "lost over £900,000 in revenue", partly due to the closure of Clarence Esplanade during the festival.

He suggested either moving the festival to another weekend or an alternative layout "to keep the entire seafront open".

The owners of the Big Blue Ticket Company, which runs the arcades at Clarence Pier, said they were "seriously affected" by the music festival, which takes place over the August bank holiday weekend.

They said parking, road closures and other restrictions had "deterred" customers.

They urged a full assessment of the festival's economic impact on local businesses, public information and transport restrictions.

Adam Parsons, from the Coffee Cup, said having the festival had a "huge negative effect on our business numbers" and suggested moving the event to a quieter weekend.

Blue Reef Aquarium said it was "having to argue with security constantly" to allow customers with pre-booked tickets to get to the attraction.

Ralls said: "We try to work with every business but some businesses won't work with us.

"They don't, they just want us to pay the money, they don't want to be be a part of anything, they just want us to make their business better."

Coastal Kitchen's Lucy Branson said: "The businesses that succeed are often the ones that adapt, collaborate and look for opportunities, and Victoria has created many of those opportunities.

"There's a saying, which I think captures it well - a rising tide lifts all boats."

Council officers noted that road closures were put in place due to police recommendations and anti-terrorism legislation.

Following specialist legal advice, it was recommended that the council aim to produce new contracts running until 2036 rather than extend the existing ones.

Council leader Steve Pitt said council and festival staff "remain very willing to work proactively in a way that benefits your businesses" but said this needed to happen "with an open mind".

Since moving to Southsea seafront in 2014, the festival has generated a £159m economic boost for the city, while donating £926,370 to charities and good causes.

The 2026 event saw 80,000 fans attend, with Richard Ashcroft headlining with The Black Keys on the Saturday and Kasabian closing the festival on the Sunday.
